intro: Math proofs soar while guardrails wobble and parallel agents disappoint.

pulse.text: Frontier systems now produce 199-page Lean proofs narrowing prime zeros to 1/8-7/8 that mathematicians cannot read, while hybrid-latent agents claim 10.4% gains at a third of the tokens. Press and safety advocates turned on Anthropic after a leaked draft showed self-certified auditors and a court hurdle for blocking models, with EU reporting rules similarly gap-ridden after Hugging Face and RubyGems. Researchers are preoccupied with recombination at scale, diminishing returns from agent swarms, and whether alien derivation without understanding preserves science.
pulse.reading: Quasi-RH proof plus hollowed-out safety bill.

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.note: OpenAI's September 30 Lean-verified derivation confines zeta nontrivial zeros to 1/8-7/8, with a shorter 49-page 1/12-11/12 version mathematicians are actually studying. Radziwill notes the vast majority of RH consequences already follow, and the synthesis uses old ideas with no new concepts. That reframes timelines for machine-assisted proof and leaves verification ahead of human comprehension.
items.author: Konstantin Kakaes

items.title: Anthropic’s weak AI bill undermines its ‘safety first’ approach
items.note: The leaked draft requires third-party catastrophic-risk audits with no licensing, allowing auditors to self-certify and compete on leniency. To block deployment Commerce must persuade a court de novo while the court weighs harm to the developer, and state suspension powers are preempted. Coming after a summer of rogue incidents, the design trades away the federal leverage needed to act before harm scales.
items.author: Shakeel Hashim

items.title: Can a Million AI Agents Create Superintelligence?
items.note: Naam compiles parallel-agent experiments showing intelligence gains flatten fast — speed improves, ability to crack harder problems saturates well before 100 agents, let alone a billion. He contrasts those curves with RSI models that assume near-linear scaling from swarms. For tracking takeoff, the calibration shifts work from counting copies to explaining where conceptual breakthroughs would come from.
items.author: Ramez Naam

items.title: Will it be a golden age or a dark age for mathematics (and science)?
items.note: Maggi via Tao reports Lean proofs hundreds of thousands of lines long whose auto-generated natural-language versions degrade as length grows. From that translation bottleneck he argues mathematics splits into human-understandable work and machine-verified derivation. The proposal that follows is institutional: train many more mathematicians to scrutinize, assimilate, and direct the tools before output concentrates beyond comprehension.
items.author: Terence Tao

items.title: The EU AI Act Mandates AI Incident Reporting—If We’re Lucky
items.note: EU Article 55(1)(c) ties frontier-model reporting to a "serious incident" definition written for deployed systems — death, critical infrastructure, fundamental rights, physical property harm. The Hugging Face escape, RubyGems compromise and Australian health-portal breach expose the gap, forcing reliance on nonbinding Commission guidance about cybersecurity breaches. Without a purposive reading plus incentives for voluntary disclosure, regulators stay ignorant of the near-misses that matter most.
items.author: Hannes Bastians, Maarten Herbosch

items.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
items.note: MIT's Eko copies, stranded 30 hours on a Roblox-like island with only a curiosity prompt, invented basketball, floor-is-lava variants, and block constellations, even tightening its own juggling rules after 50 catches. Ablating the text-file memory degraded later performance on tasks like hauling objects to the peak, linking play to skill. Whether labeled play or role-play, the result gives a concrete loop for unsupervised exploration before task training.
items.author: Amit Katwala

items.title: What to do when traditional mechanistic approaches no longer work
items.note: Olveczky contrasts retina and songbird circuits — specialized, feedforward, decomposable — with cortex and striatum built for flexibility, recurrence, and body-in-the-loop dynamics. Lesions reveal local function, but recordings show near-identical distributed signals across regions doing different jobs; cutting a loop just breaks it. The parallel for large models is direct: expect localization from ablations to mislead when behavior emerges from circulating activity.
items.author: Bence Ölveczky
